summary.text: Suzan DelBene is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 1st District, first elected in 2012. Before Congress she was a technology executive and entrepreneur and then director of the Washington State Department of Revenue. She serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and chaired the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee for the 2024 cycle.

paragraphs.text: DelBene was born in Selma, Alabama, in 1962. According to her official biography, she spent part of her early childhood in Newport Hills and Mercer Island, Washington, before her father lost his job and the family moved around the country in search of work.
She earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Reed College in 1983 and an MBA from the University of Washington in 1990.

Her official biography says she began her career in immunology research before moving into business, where she helped start drugstore.com and spent 12 years at Microsoft, most recently as corporate vice president of its mobile communications business.

She later served as CEO and president of Nimble Technology, a business software company built on technology developed at the University of Washington, and worked as a consultant for Global Partnerships.

DelBene served as director of the Washington State Department of Revenue. Her official biography says she proposed reforms to cut red tape for small businesses and enacted a tax amnesty program that generated $345 million.
She ran for Congress in Washington's 8th District in 2010 and lost to incumbent Republican Dave Reichert.

In 2012 she won a special election to fill the remainder of Jay Inslee's term and the regular election for the redrawn 1st District, and she was first sworn in to the House in November 2012. She has been re-elected since.

In the House, DelBene serves on the Committee on Ways and Means and its Tax, Trade, and Oversight subcommittees. She co-chairs the Women's High-Tech Coalition, Kidney Caucus, and MedTech Caucus, and chaired the New Democrat Coalition in the 117th Congress.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries appointed her in December 2022 as chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee for the 2024 election cycle.
Her official biography lists among her legislative accomplishments two laws addressing the baby formula shortage and the National Landslide Preparedness Act.
